turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. I'll grab your blood pressure before the doctor comes in. Was the freeway a nightmare?
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Absolute shocker. Forty minutes on the Gateway and the air-con dying. We nearly turned around.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): It was rather slow, yes. I apologise if that has put us behind.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): You're fine. Arm straight, please.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is 142 over 88. Pulse 76. Sats 98 percent. Pop back in the chair.
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): Thank you. I hope those figures are acceptable.
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor will go through them. He won't be long.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): Mr Hale. Dr Okonkwo. What's the problem today?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): Good morning, doctor. I have had headaches for many years, but the pattern has altered, and I felt I should have it reviewed.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): How many years?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): Ten years, I believe. They were diagnosed as migraine by my previous GP.
[SEG0012] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's fifteen if it's a day. He had them when we moved in together, well before ten years.
[SEG0013] person_4 (DOCTOR): So ten to fifteen years, not pinned down. One side or both?
[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): Across the forehead, and at times behind the right eye. Previously they were strictly one-sided.
[SEG0015] person_4 (DOCTOR): Time of day?
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): These recent ones are clearly worse on waking, in the morning. I cannot date when that shift began. A few months, perhaps. I am not sure.
[SEG0017] person_4 (DOCTOR): Vomiting with them?
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): No. I do not vomit.
[SEG0019] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry, the parking app just— oh, never mind, go on.
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): Forgive me, I spoke too quickly. There were two mornings this month when I was actually sick. I had put them out of my mind.
[SEG0021] person_4 (DOCTOR): And the build-up, is it sudden or—
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): It comes on over about twenty minutes, and then it sort of—
[SEG0023] person_4 (DOCTOR): Plateaus?
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes. It plateaus, rather than striking all at once.
[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): How many mornings a week?
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): Four or five days out of seven. The older migraines were only twice a month.
[SEG0027] person_4 (DOCTOR): Score out of ten?
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): Around seven. On a bad morning, eight.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any blurring or double vision?
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): No. My sight remains clear.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): Weakness, numbness, or trouble speaking?
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): None of those.
[SEG0033] person_4 (DOCTOR): Fever or a stiff neck?
[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): No fever, and the neck is not stiff.
[SEG0035] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any previous surgery?
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): None. I have never had an operation.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): What are you taking?
[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): Sumatriptan, and paracetamol. I have used the sumatriptan for a long time.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): What dose is the sumatriptan?
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): Fifty milligrams, I believe, one tablet by mouth at the onset.
[SEG0041] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's not. The Imigran box is one hundred milligrams. I've seen him take it.
[SEG0042] person_3 (PATIENT): Then I must stand corrected, or perhaps both strengths have been in the house. I honestly cannot say which I am using now.
[SEG0043] person_4 (DOCTOR): Every attack?
[SEG0044] person_3 (PATIENT): On most headache days. If I have to drive to the office I leave it, because it can make me a little spaced.
[SEG0045] person_4 (DOCTOR): Paracetamol dose?
[SEG0046] person_3 (PATIENT): Two tablets of five hundred milligrams, by mouth, when the pain begins. Seldom more than twice in one day.

[SEG0047] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He gets the large packs from the chemist. My sister is forever offering him her biotin gummies, swears they fix her energy, but he doesn't take her tablets. Different person entirely.
[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any other regular medicines of yours?
[SEG0049] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Nothing else of mine.
[SEG0050] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His brother, though, type two diabetes, metformin morning and night. Not our problem today, I know.
[SEG0051] person_4 (DOCTOR): Medicine allergies?
[SEG0052] person_3 (PATIENT): I cannot be precise. An antibiotic years ago brought me out in a rash. The name escapes me. I have avoided guessing since.
[SEG0053] person_4 (DOCTOR): Do you snore?
[SEG0054] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Loudly, every night. And by mid-arvo he is wrecked, asleep on the lounge if he sits down.
[SEG0055] person_3 (PATIENT): I do not snore, doctor. I must respectfully disagree. I am a little weary after lunch, I will allow that, but I am not falling asleep.
[SEG0056] person_4 (DOCTOR): Have you nodded off while driving?
[SEG0057] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Last month on the freeway he drifted over the line. I grabbed the wheel.
[SEG0058] person_3 (PATIENT): That was congestion, not sleep. I was entirely awake, and I do not accept that account.
[SEG0059] person_4 (DOCTOR): Weight up or down? Up at night to pass urine?
[SEG0060] person_3 (PATIENT): Weight is unchanged. I rise once a night to pass urine, and I have done so for years.
[SEG0061] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Before we forget, that storm last night took the branch off the jacaranda. The cricket was a write-off too.
[SEG0062] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, the first session looked promising before the covers came on. A rather slow pitch, I thought.
[SEG0063] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): My grandson had a scorecard going. Seven, and already shouting about LBW. He wants to bowl leg spin.
[SEG0064] person_3 (PATIENT): We said we might fetch him that Gray-Nicolls bat on Saturday, if the humidity eases and the sports shop is open.
[SEG0065] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): If the Melbourne weather clears he wants the highlights as well. I told him not to hold his breath. The outfield was a lake.
[SEG0066] person_3 (PATIENT): He will survive the disappointment. The drive home may be slower if another storm sits on the motorway.
[SEG0067] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's already arguing with the third umpire on the replay. I told him that's just cricket.
[SEG0068] person_3 (PATIENT): We had the same debate over the tea interval. It can wait until Saturday.
[SEG0069] person_4 (DOCTOR): Enough of the weather. On the bed. Look at my finger.
[SEG0070] person_4 (DOCTOR): Pupils equal and reactive. Face symmetrical. No droop.
[SEG0071] person_4 (DOCTOR): Grip hard. Full power, both hands. Legs the same, pushing me away. Equal.
[SEG0072] person_4 (DOCTOR): Reflexes symmetrical. Finger-nose is fine. No tremor. Quick look in the eyes, no papilloedema. Neuro exam is normal.
[SEG0073] person_3 (PATIENT): I am glad to hear that.

[SEG0074] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'm running through possibilities, not a diagnosis. Could be the migraine shifting to the mornings. Could be fragmented sleep, if the snoring is real. Could be a mass, with morning pain and vomiting. I am not concluding any of that, and I will not call it sleep apnoea or a tumour today.
[SEG0075] person_3 (PATIENT): I appreciate you being direct.
[SEG0076] person_4 (DOCTOR): If the morning headaches and vomiting have not settled in a fortnight, I will arrange an MRI of the brain. If they settle, no scan.
[SEG0077] person_3 (PATIENT): And a review in any case?
[SEG0078] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes. I want to see you in three weeks, settle or not.
[SEG0079] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Does he stop the sumatriptan in the meantime?
[SEG0080] person_4 (DOCTOR): No. Use it at the start of the headache. Check which strength is in the box tonight and bring that box next visit. Paracetamol, no more than eight tablets in a day.
[SEG0081] person_3 (PATIENT): I shall check the box and I shall keep to eight. Thank you.
[SEG0082] person_4 (DOCTOR): If you get a sudden worst headache of your life, new weakness, or confusion, go straight to emergency. Don't wait three weeks.
[SEG0083] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): What about the snoring he won't own up to?
[SEG0084] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'm still not diagnosing it. No driving if you feel drowsy. Off you go.

features: tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.

third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
